ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-04-15
Provider: Dr. James Okafor, MD
Department: Nephrology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive swelling in lower legs and increasing fatigue with foamy, dark urine

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 45-year-old male with hereditary hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, and chronic kidney disease stage 3, previously evaluated in January for fatigue and joint discomfort, returns to clinic with his wife reporting progressive swelling in his lower legs and increasing fatigue over the past month. He also reports that his urine has been "foamy" and occasionally darker than usual.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Hereditary Hemochromatosis with arthropathy (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Hereditary hemochromatosis
- Wilson disease
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Chronic kidney disease stage 3
- Cirrhosis
- Obesity

The patient was diagnosed with Wilson disease 6 years ago after presenting with abnormal liver function tests and neurologic symptoms, including mild dysarthria and tremor. Since diagnosis, he has been managed with dietary copper restriction and a chelating agent. His dose of the chelating agent was increased 5 months ago due to rising urinary copper levels on follow-up testing.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Dental extraction
- Therapeutic phlebotomy (maintenance)

MEDICATIONS:
He has been adherent to all medications and has not recently started any new drugs.

Home Medications:
- Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
- Trientine 500 mg twice daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Furosemide 40 mg daily

ALLERGIES:
Amoxicillin (drug-induced hemolytic anemia), Penicillin

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Brother with Wilson disease
- Paternal uncle with hemochromatosis
- Father with type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Mother with hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 8 years ago. Alcohol: History of chronic alcohol use disorder, currently abstinent for 3 years. Occupation: Automotive mechanic.

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure is 130/78 mm Hg, pulse is 78/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical exam reveals periorbital puffiness and 2+ bilateral pitting edema to the mid-shins. Cardiopulmonary examination is normal, and there are no rashes or joint swelling. Abdominal exam shows mild hepatomegaly without tenderness or ascites. No pulmonary crackles are heard, and there is no jugular venous distension.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies show a serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL and serum albumin of 2.2 g/dL Urinalysis shows 4+ protein, no red blood cells, no white blood cells and no casts. A 24-hour urine protein demonstrates 5.8 g/day.

PATHOLOGY:
Immunofluorescence demonstrates fine granular deposits of IgG and C3 along the glomerular capillary wall.
